6465-short-cruises.title: Short Cruises
6465-short-cruises.creator: W. W. Jacobs
6465-short-cruises.description: A book by W. W. Jacobs. George Henshaw let himself in at the front door, and stood for some time wiping his boots on the mat. The little house was ominously still, and a faint feeling, only partially due to the lapse of time since breakfast, manifested itself behind his waistcoat. He coughed—a matter-of-fact cough—and, with an attempt to hum a tune, hung his hat on the peg and entered the kitchen.

arxiv-2106-06017.title: Cross-lingual Emotion Detection
arxiv-2106-06017.description: Abstract Emotion detection can provide us with a window into understanding human behavior. Due to the complex dynamics of human emotions, however, constructing annotated datasets to train automated models can be expensive. Thus, we explore the efficacy of cross-lingual approaches that would use data from a source language to build models for emotion detection in a target language.

arxiv-2202-04092.title: Machine Explanations and Human Understanding
arxiv-2202-04092.creator: Chacha Chen* chacha@uchicago.edu, Shi Feng* shif@uchicago.edu, Amit Sharma amshar@microsoft.com, Chenhao Tan chenhao@uchicago.edu
arxiv-2202-04092.description: Abstract Explanations are hypothesized to improve human understanding of machine learning models and achieve a variety of desirable outcomes, ranging from model debugging to enhancing human decision making. However, empirical studies have found mixed and even negative results. An open question, therefore, is under what conditions explanations can improve human understanding and in what way .

arxiv-2306-04567.title: Eisenstein congruences among Euler systems
arxiv-2306-04567.creator: Óscar Rivero and Victor Rotger
arxiv-2306-04567.description: Abstract . We investigate Eisenstein congruences between the so-called Euler systems of Garrett–Rankin–Selberg type. This includes the cohomology classes of Beilinson–Kato, Beilinson–Flach and diagonal cycles. The proofs crucially rely on different known versions of the Bloch–Kato conjecture, and are based on the study of the Perrin-Riou formalism and the comparison between the different p p -adic L L -functions.

arxiv-2401-12766.title: Absorbing ideals: a survey on ω \omega -stable groups
arxiv-2401-12766.creator: Bruno Moreira Fernandes
arxiv-2401-12766.description: Abstract We introduce a new concept in the Absorbing Ideal Theory in commutative rings, that is, the ω \omega -stable groups. We will provide examples and non-examples of these groups, and establish their relationship with H H -congruence. Ultimately, we will study the action of these groups considering the transitivity condition. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 13A15, 13A50.

arxiv-2502-10043.title: Generalized Uncertainty Principle mimicking dynamical Dark Energy: matter perturbations and gravitational wave data analysis
arxiv-2502-10043.creator: G. G. Luciano, Y. Sekhmani
arxiv-2502-10043.description: Abstract The Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) stands out as a nearly ubiquitous feature in quantum gravity modeling, predicting the emergence of a minimum length at the Planck scale. Recently, it has been shown to modify the area-law scaling of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, giving rise to deformed Friedmann equations within Jacobson’s approach.

arxiv-2503-14855.title: Sensorized gripper for human demonstrations
arxiv-2503-14855.creator: Sri Harsha Turlapati, Gautami Golani, Mohammad Zaidi Ariffin, Domenico Campolo
arxiv-2503-14855.description: Abstract Ease of programming is a key factor in making robots ubiquitous in unstructured environments. In this work, we present a sensorized gripper built with off-the-shelf parts, used to record human demonstrations of a box in box assembly task. With very few trials of short interval timings each, we show that a robot can repeat the task successfully.

arxiv-2506-23913.title: On morphisms of topological quivers
arxiv-2506-23913.creator: Mariusz Tobolski
arxiv-2506-23913.description: Abstract We introduce regular morphisms of topological quivers and show that they give rise to a subcategory of the category of topological quivers and quiver morphisms. Our regularity conditions render the topological quiver C*-algebra construction a contravariant functor from the category of topological quivers and regular morphisms into the category of C*-algebras and ∗ * -homomorphisms.

arxiv-2508-14197.title: CLIPSym: Delving into Symmetry Detection with CLIP
arxiv-2508-14197.creator: Tinghan Yang, Md Ashiqur Rahman, Raymond A. Yeh
arxiv-2508-14197.description: Abstract Symmetry is one of the most fundamental geometric cues in computer vision, and detecting it has been an ongoing challenge. With the recent advances in vision-language models, i.e., CLIP, we investigate whether a pre-trained CLIP model can aid symmetry detection by leveraging the additional symmetry cues found in the natural image descriptions.

pmc-10597194.description: The EU has approved a proposal for a Joint Action on Cancer and other NCDs prevention - action on health determinants. This is a large and ambitious initiative with more than 20 participating EU member states along with Iceland, Norway, and Ukraine.

pmc-10643983.title: Linear alopecia in pediatrics: RCM and dermoscopy reveal diagnostic cues
pmc-10643983.creator: Ying Wang, Lixin Chen, Bei Qin, Qinfeng Li
pmc-10643983.description: BackgroundAlopecia areata (AA), trichotillomania (TM), nevus sebaceous (NS), and linear scleroderma en coup de sabre (LSCS) can all present with a patch of linear alopecia, making diagnosis challenging. The purpose of this study was to combine reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) and dermoscopy in the diagnosis of these lesions in children.

pmc-11712402.title: Unraveling the Link Between SGLT2 Inhibition, Circulating Metabolites, and Alzheimer’s Dementia: A Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11712402.creator: Hao Yang, Yuye Ning, Meilin Chen, Jianping Jia
pmc-11712402.description: BackgroundIndividuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face an increased risk of dementia. Recent discoveries indicate that SGLT2 inhibitors, a newer class of anti‐diabetic medication, exhibit beneficial metabolic effects beyond glucose control, offering a potential avenue for mitigating the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD).

pmc-12473508.title: A Tactile Cognitive Model Based on Correlated Texture Information Entropy and Multimodal Fusion Learning
pmc-12473508.creator: Si Chen, Chi Gao, Chen Chen, Weimin Ru, Ning Yang, Aiguo Song
pmc-12473508.description: (1) Background: Multimodal tactile cognition is paramount for robotic dexterity, yet its advancement is constrained by the limited realism of existing texture datasets and the difficulty of effectively fusing heterogeneous signals. This study introduces a comprehensive framework to overcome these limitations by integrating a parametrically designed dataset with a novel fusion architecture.

pmc-12529311.title: Criterion Validity of the Problematic Khat Use Screening Tool (PKUST-17) in Ethiopia
pmc-12529311.creator: Awoke Mihretu, Solomon Teferra, Yohannes Gebreegziabhere, Kassahun Habtamu, Abebaw Fekadu
pmc-12529311.description: BackgroundThe use of amphetamine-type stimulants such as khat has been spreading quickly in eastern parts of Africa, the Arabian region and Asia. However, screening for the provision of early intervention has been inadequate, primarily because of the lack of culturally acceptable and valid screening tools.

pmc-12998386.title: Epidemiological Risk Factor Analysis for Maternal Mortality Associated with Eclampsia: A Single-Center Study from Tertiary Hospital Garut
pmc-12998386.creator: Dadan Susandi, Rizky Alamsyah Martani, Putri Nadhira Adinda Adriansyah, Annisa Dewi Nugrahani, Dhanny Primantara Johari Santoso, Yunia Sribudiani, Ruswana Anwar, Johanes Cornelius Mose
pmc-12998386.description: BackgroundMaternal mortality remains a major global health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Eclampsia, a severe complication of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, continues to contribute substantially to maternal and perinatal deaths despite advances in obstetric care. Previous studies have highlighted the role of clinical and laboratory abnormalities in worsening outcomes; however, evidence from developing settings remains limited.

pmc-13096030.title: Causal Relationship Between 38 Dietary Factors, Including Sugar and Alcohol Intakes, and Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-13096030.creator: Le Xu, Sa Zhang, Wanting Shi, Shien Zou
pmc-13096030.description: PurposeEmerging evidence suggests that diets high in sugar consumption may be implicated in the development of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), but the causal nature of these associations remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the potential causal links between 38 specific dietary factors (including alcohol and added sugar), particularly sugar-sweetened beverage intake, and the risk of PCOS.

pmc-13224459.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and associations of soil organic carbon and total nitrogen in the Qilian Mountain Grasslands
pmc-13224459.creator: Jiafang Cai, Meiling Zhang, Youyi Zhao, Yanjun Gong, Hanying Wang
pmc-13224459.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding the coordinated changes in soil carbon and nitrogen is essential for evaluating ecosystem responses to environmental change, particularly in ecologically fragile alpine regions such as the Qilian Mountains. In this study, the denitrification–decomposition (DNDC) model was used to assess the spatiotemporal dynamics of soil organic carbon density (SOCD) and total nitrogen density (STND) in the 0–30 cm soil layer from 1975 to 2024.
